title: Leveraging Contextual Counterfactuals Toward Belief Calibration

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the counterfactual recourse cost (the minimal effort or cost required for an individual to change a negative decision to a positive one) in a credit classification task, specifically penalizing models that require changes to non-actionable demographic features (like age or marital status).

Using a multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework to evaluate how differently calibrated model beliefs (priors on noise, sparsity, and decision leniency) impact predictive accuracy versus the severity of societal consequences (measured via false negative and true negative recourse costs).
